previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted for acute respiratory failure and hypertensive emergency leading to pulmonary edema. She presented with severe dyspnea and was initially managed in the MICU with CPAP and IV furosemide, resulting in significant improvement. Her condition was complicated by medication noncompliance and a high pill burden, which contributed to fluid overload. Antibiotics were briefly administered due to leukocytosis but discontinued as infection was ruled out. She transitioned to the medicine floor, where her heart failure and asthma were managed with optimized medications, including initiation of lisinopril, carvedilol, and fluticasone-salmeterol. Her chest X-ray showed complete resolution of pulmonary opacities. Medication reconciliation simplified her regimen. She remained in sinus rhythm throughout. Discharge planning included a steroid taper, follow-up for gangrene with vascular surgery, and coordination with her primary care provider for ongoing management of anemia, hyperlipidemia, and advance care planning. She was discharged home with services in stable condition.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Chest, single frontal view.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Tachycardia, rule out CHF.

___.

FINDINGS:  Single frontal view of the chest was obtained.  There is persistent
elevation of the right hemidiaphragm in this patient status post right upper
lobe lobectomy.  The left lung is clear.  No new focal consolidation, pleural
effusion, or evidence of pneumothorax is seen.  Cardiac and mediastinal
silhouettes are stable.  Partially imaged right humeral prosthesis is seen.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary process.

INDICATION:  Necrotic toes.  Evaluate for osteomyelitis.

COMPARISON:  None.


THREE VIEWS, RIGHT FOOT:

There is mild metatarsus varus/hallux valgus deformity.  Mild degenerative
changes are noted of the first MTP joint.  Claw toe deformities are noted of
the second through fifth digits.  Mild degenerative changes of the
interphalangeal and tarsometatarsal joints.  No definite osteolysis or
periosteal reaction.  There are small plantar calcaneal spurs and vascular
calcifications.

THREE VIEWS, LEFT FOOT:

There is mild metatarsus varus/hallux valgus and degenerative changes of the
first metatarsophalangeal joint.  Chronic fifth proximal phalanx fracture. 
There is no definite periosteal reaction or osteolysis.  There is a small
plantar calcaneal spur and vascular calcifications.

IMPRESSION:  No definite radiographic evidence of osteomyelitis.  If there is
high continued clinical concern, MRI can be considered.
